added_claims.speaker: Kristalina Georgieva
added_claims.quote: We have lending capacity of $1 trillion. We deploy it for countries in crisis.
added_claims.claim: The IMF's role is to lend quickly (capacity about $1 trillion) to finance balance-of-payments needs of countries in crisis, not to fund investment projects, so it acts as a cushion that stops a country 'about to crash'.
added_claims.conditions: when markets close to a country or reserves run out

added_claims.speaker: Kristalina Georgieva
added_claims.quote: The best value from the fund is to put in place good policies and responsible institutions.
added_claims.claim: The IMF argues the lasting benefit comes from good policies and responsible institutions that let a country grow on its own after the emergency cushion, rather than from repeated bailouts.
added_claims.direction: better institutions lead to a better growth trajectory
added_claims.conditions: countries that implement the reforms attached to programs
added_claims.testable: partly - program outcomes can be compared but selection is severe

added_claims.speaker: Kristalina Georgieva
added_claims.quote: We are like a savings bank. Countries commit resources to the fund. Then we lend this money.
added_claims.claim: The IMF is funded by member quotas that it lends out and is repaid with interest, with no taxpayer contributions, which lets it commit large sums very quickly in a crisis.

added_claims.speaker: Kristalina Georgieva
added_claims.quote: they hold over 17% of the quarters of the IMF and in that sense they are the only member that has v2 power
added_claims.claim: The US holds over 17% of IMF quotas and so is the only member with a veto, because major decisions require at least 85% of the vote; global crisis support therefore depends on US consent.

added_claims.speaker: Kristalina Georgieva
added_claims.quote: Europe has done a very good job in bringing inflation to target.
added_claims.claim: Inflation in Europe is back at target, while US disinflation is slower and exposed to tariff pass-through, so the IMF sees the inflation threat as more contained in Europe.
added_claims.testable: yes - compare inflation prints with targets

added_claims.speaker: Kristalina Georgieva
added_claims.quote: financial stability risks that are related to either the economy changing rapidly uh which by the way seems to be now a slower process to decarbonization
added_claims.claim: Climate-related financial stability risk has a transition channel (rapid economic change) and a physical channel (shocks to businesses and households); the transition channel looks smaller now because decarbonization is proceeding more slowly.
added_claims.testable: partly - transition risk scenarios can be stress-tested

added_claims.speaker: Kristalina Georgieva
added_claims.quote: countries that have the um comparative advantage, cheap energy, preferably renewable energy, um high level of investment in research and development, they have responsibility to move the frontier
added_claims.claim: Countries with cheap (preferably renewable) energy and high R&D investment have the comparative advantage to push the AI frontier, which links AI capacity to energy cost and research spending.
added_claims.direction: AI leadership favors cheap-energy, high-R&D economies
added_claims.testable: partly - cross-country AI investment against energy cost and R&D

added_claims.speaker: Kristalina Georgieva
added_claims.quote: what is um different today is that getting uh cooperation uh takes more more effort
added_claims.claim: Coordinated crisis response is harder to assemble now than in COVID, when emergency meetings produced a fast joint response, so the next shock may meet a slower and less coordinated policy reaction, especially with no fiscal buffers.
